title: Pre-Export Row Scaling for Generated Mixed-Integer Programs: Accuracy Contracts and Software Evaluation

creators.name: Rodríguez Castro, Mathias
creators.affiliation: Facultad de Ingeniería, Universidad de la República, Montevideo, Uruguay

description: Locally frozen OMS submission snapshot for the manuscript "Pre-Export Row Scaling for Generated Mixed-Integer Programs: Accuracy Contracts and Software Evaluation". Supplied as Supplementary Material 2; this metadata prepares a possible later deposition and does not assert publication or assign a DOI. Reuses the v1.2-coap-submission historical baseline (10.5281/zenodo.23145294) and adds a controlled 30-model Base/Flat-GM/Ruiz-R4/Role-Hybrid comparison, a six-model final-policy implementation check (132 assigned runs in total), and a three-scenario physical-budget audit of 129,600 rows per policy. A focused activation follow-up adds 114 nonpilot calls, 20 independently checked exact feasible witnesses, and preset sensitivity; it distinguishes primal precision from MILP-bound validity. An auxiliary common-incumbent diagnostic retains 36 MILP calls, three exact reference LPs and 15 subsequent fixed-pattern LP checks, including two unknown outcomes; it qualifies mechanism attribution without a new principal contribution or a general speedup claim. A matched IntegralityFocus control and complete fresh-process workflow measurement retain 12 principal calls and 12 instrumentation calls with identical native endpoints, under a declared shared-machine timing limitation. A fully matched six-model accuracy/remedy comparison adds 144 terminal comparisons under automatic/off presolve and 145 native attempts including one retained external interruption. It keeps budget delivery, native effort and independently refuted bounds distinct. All new LP exports, named bases, factors, native logs, incumbents, unit conversions and replay scripts are included. The exact Supplementary Material 1 PDF is included. Only the complete historical 1,530-basis reconstruction requires the separate baseline bulk archive. Code: MIT; data and results: CC BY 4.0; manuscript: outside those licenses. No external financial funding or research grant; historical ClusterUY computing resources are acknowledged. Journal submission, acceptance and publication are not claimed. Version v1.3.11 adds a prespecified seven-budget sensitivity (330 MILP calls and 30 abstentions), an isolated C++ selector preparation benchmark with exactly matching exports, and exact global-LP reference intervals for the six original Base models. Three reference integer witnesses are certified within 1%, including one exact MILP optimum. These do not certify every native floating-export result. The broader joint row/column research remains separate from the manuscript claims. Version v1.3.12 is an editorial-only revision: it foregrounds the existing 30–100 m3 precision–effort regime in the abstract, introduction and main Table 12, and corrects the stated scope of exact dispatch reference certification. It adds no research solver calls. The regime remains specific to six known models from one application family; zero detected contradictions is not a general MILP optimality certificate. Version v1.3.13 (17 October 2026) adds bounded independent batch-scheduling transfer (96 comparisons and eight reference MIPs), an integer-tolerance control (36 new MIPs, 54 reused calls and 18 abstentions), and a 36-call paired native complete-cycle benchmark. There are 176 new MIP calls and eight exact-reference LP attempts. One external exact reference succeeds; seven are unresolved, leaving 84 comparison-bound checks unknown. Budget-L2 and matched L2 each meet all 24 external primal budgets; NF3 meets 23. All 18 native implementation pairs have identical data, points, work and endpoints; paired C++/Python full-time ratio is 0.824 on the shared host. The zero-bound-contradiction dispatch regime is not robust to both integer tolerances. No general MILP optimality or universal speedup is claimed. The author confirmed CAP did not support this work. Version v1.3.14 foregrounds the software workflow and adds a secondary audit without new optimizer calls. At the two tested favorable dispatch targets, all 36 paired work comparisons favor Budget-L2 over NF3; deleting any one observed model or seed retains the aggregate advantage. External Budget-L2/L2 work and complete-time ratios are 0.960 and 1.054; transfer of numerical budgets does not establish external computational superiority. All adverse settings, unknown bound checks and the limits of internal mechanism attribution are retained.
